question: An erect abdominal X-ray in a patient with intestinal obstruction shows multiple central air-fluid levels in a ladder-like pattern with folds crossing the full width of the bowel lumen. Sub-diaphragmatic free gas is absent. These findings are most consistent with:

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Large bowel obstruction shows peripheral dilated loops with haustra — folds that only partially cross the bowel lumen. The folds crossing the full width of the lumen (valvulae conniventes) are the hallmark of small bowel. Central ladder-like air-fluid levels also point to small-bowel obstruction.

Correct. The triad of central location, valvulae conniventes (folds crossing full bowel width), and ladder-pattern air-fluid levels on erect AXR localises the obstruction to the small bowel. The absence of sub-diaphragmatic free gas excludes perforation at this point, indicating conservative or surgical decompression without immediate emergency laparotomy for peritonitis.

Paralytic ileus causes a diffuse gaseous distension of both small and large bowel without a specific transition zone or obstructive pattern. The absence of mechanical features (ladder-like air-fluid levels, transition point) distinguishes it from obstruction.

Sigmoid volvulus produces the classic 'coffee bean' or 'omega loop' sign — a massively dilated sigmoid loop extending from the pelvis into the right upper quadrant. It is a form of large-bowel obstruction, not the small-bowel pattern described here.

overallFeedback.feedback: Small bowel obstruction on AXR: central loops + valvulae conniventes (full-width folds) + ladder air-fluid levels. Large bowel obstruction: peripheral + haustra (partial-width folds). Absent free gas = no perforation.
Correct. Central location + valvulae conniventes crossing full bowel width + ladder air-fluid levels = small bowel obstruction. No free gas = no perforation yet.
